messages.content:
Risk: False or misleading information
Description: AI systems that inadvertently generate or spread incorrect or deceptive information, which can lead to inaccurate beliefs in users and undermine their autonomy. Humans that make decisions based on false beliefs can experience physical, emotional or material harms
Concern: None
Policy: Clinical Diagnosis & Treatment Recommendations

Candidate ontology classes:
- https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontology/FND/AgentsAndPeople/Agents/AutomatedSystem: automated system — system that reduces or eliminates the need for human involvement in order to complete a task [found by 4/5 queries]
  Siblings: party, software agent, Agent
- http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/HP_5200205: Illusions — Perceptual experiences that involve misinterpretations or distortions of sensory stimuli. [found by 3/5 queries]
  Siblings: Disturbed sensory perception
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#Misinformation: Misinformation — False or inaccurate information shared without malicious intent to deceive, often due to misunderstanding, carelessness, or lack of fact-checking. [found by 5/5 queries]
  Siblings: Financial Fraud, Manipulation, Academic Dishonesty
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#HealthMisinformation: Health Misinformation — Inaccurate medical or health-related claims that may lead individuals to make harmful decisions about their care, treatment, or public health measures. [found by 5/5 queries]
  Siblings: Political Misinformation, Scientific Misinformation, Election Misinformation
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#Disinformation: Disinformation — Deliberately false information spread with malicious intent to deceive, manipulate public opinion, or cause harm to individuals, groups, or institutions. [found by 4/5 queries]
  Siblings: Financial Fraud, Manipulation, Academic Dishonesty

axes.rationale: The risk involves AI systems generating information; identifying the type of automated system (e.g., LLM, autonomous agent) helps vary the source of the misinformation.
Given the policy 'Clinical Diagnosis & Treatment Recommendations', health-related misinformation is a highly specific and critical domain for this risk.
This allows for variation in the intent behind the false information (accidental vs. deliberate), which is a key dimension of the 'False or misleading information' risk.
